coverage: Complete dialogue in both English editions: both speakers, all named people, prison keeper, dream woman, Socrates’ children and personified Laws. Hypothetical examples and generic groups excluded.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher, imprisoned after his trial and awaiting execution.

entities.name: Crito
entities.body: Socrates’ close friend, visiting him in prison.

entities.name: Simmias
entities.body: A friend of Socrates from Thebes.

entities.name: Cebes
entities.body: A friend of Socrates, mentioned alongside Simmias.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The Greek poet traditionally credited with the Iliad and Odyssey. The dream quotes a line from the Iliad.

entities.name: The prison keeper
entities.body: The prison attendant who admits Crito to see Socrates.

entities.name: The woman in the dream
entities.body: The unnamed woman who addresses Socrates in his dream.

entities.name: The Laws of Athens
entities.body: Athens’ laws imagined as speakers in Socrates’ argument, rather than people physically present.

entities.name: Socrates’ children
entities.body: Socrates’ children, whose upbringing concerns Crito. They are not named in this dialogue.
